new_statements.quote: 【哈尼语】属汉藏语系藏缅语族彝语 ... 一般无辅音韵尾,个别地区有-ŋ ,或-m 韵尾。有 4 个声调,其中中升调仅出现在汉语词 ... 重音落在词的最后一音节上。有名、形、数、量、代、动、副、后置、连接、语气、语助、感叹、摹拟等 13 类词 (ellipses are Google's snippet cuts)
new_statements.translation: [Hani] belongs to the Yi branch of Tibeto-Burman, Sino-Tibetan ... generally no consonant finals, a few areas have -ŋ or -m finals. Four tones, of which the mid-rising tone occurs only in Chinese loanwords ... Stress falls on the last syllable of the word. There are 13 word classes: nouns, adjectives, numerals, classifiers, pronouns, verbs, adverbs, postpositions, conjunctions, modal, auxiliary, interjection and onomatopoeic words.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the last syllable of the word (Hani in general; the source treats Haoni-Baihong as a dialect of that language). No Honi-specific stress statement was found in any accessible source.
new_statements.exceptions: None in the snippets; 语言文字学常用辞典 hedges with 多 ('mostly'), 中国文化大典 with 一般 ('generally').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('词的最后一音节'); the entry describes Hani as a whole with the Lüchun Dazhai standard (hani1248, Ha-Ya dialect) as its reference point, and explicitly lists 豪白方言 (Haoni + Baihong) as one of its three dialects — so the claim covers Honi only by subsumption, not by a Honi-specific observation.
new_statements.identity_note: Honi [how] = Chinese 豪白方言 (Hao-Bai dialect of Hani): 豪尼 Haoni (Mojiang, Yuanjiang, Pu'er) + 白宏 Baihong (Glottolog dialect baih1238); the Woni (窝尼) of Xinping/Yangwu described by Yuan 1947, Gao 1955 and Yang 2016 is a further sub-variety whose dialect affiliation Yang 2016 ch. 10 treats as an open question. The only stress statement found is for Hani as a whole (hani1248, Lüchun Dazhai standard), not for Honi. Glottolog ref 547818 author 'Cài, Jíyàn' is wrong: CNKI names 杨艳 (Yang Yan).

tone_statements.citation: 李永燧 [Li Yongsui]. 1990. 哈尼语语法 [A grammar of Hani]. 北京: 民族出版社. 252 pp.
tone_statements.quote: ( 3 )声调方面本族固有语词一般只有高平、中平和低降三个声调,各地的读法大体一致。有的地区有曲折调或升调。升调(中升或高升)在固有语词里往往是连读变音或表示某种语法意义(如豪尼话人称代词宾格读 135 调) ,但以拼读现代汉语借词去声字为最常见。 1.2.2 下面简要介绍绿春大寨哈尼话的语音系统
tone_statements.translation: (3) As for tones, native words generally have only three tones — high level, mid level and low falling — pronounced much the same in all areas. Some areas have a contour tone or a rising tone. In native words the rising tone (mid-rising or high-rising) is usually a sandhi form or marks a grammatical meaning (e.g. in Haoni the accusative of personal pronouns is read with tone 35 ['135' is the snippet scanned of the tone-letter + 35]), but it is most common in reading modern Chinese loanwords of the departing tone. 1.2.2 Below, a brief introduction to the sound system of Lüchun Dazhai Hani.
tone_statements.locator: Ch. 1, §1.2.1 item (3) 声调, just before §1.2.2

tone.translation: (3) As for tones, native words generally have only three tones — high level, mid level and low falling — pronounced much the same in all areas. Some areas have a contour tone or a rising tone. In native words the rising tone (mid-rising or high-rising) is usually a sandhi form or marks a grammatical meaning (e.g. in Haoni the accusative of personal pronouns is read with tone 35 ['135' is the snippet scanned of the tone-letter + 35]), but it is most common in reading modern Chinese loanwords of the departing tone. 1.2.2 Below, a brief introduction to the sound system of Lüchun Dazhai Hani.
